svg.aria-label: How to write ੜ · ਘ · ਦ: 3 letters, ੜ, ਘ, ਦ, one after another
svg.title: Writing ੜ · ਘ · ਦ
svg.desc: 3 letters written one after another: ੜ, ਘ, ਦ (gurmukhi). Each letter has its own group of frames; frame N of a group shows movements 1 to N of that letter, the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansGurmukhi-Static.ttf. Each letter is drawn at its own scale from its own cited stroke order, so the strip does not show how large the letters are next to each other, how far apart they sit, or any join between them. Stroke order: ੜ: GNPS, Gurmukhi Sikho (GNPS Learning Hub), Alphabet Tracing lesson, ੜ (rhaarhaa) checkpoints, strokes 1–3 (lib/data/lessons/lesson_tracing.dart line 1108, commit de1e560; Apache-2.0) <https://github.com/codemanxdev/gnps_learning_hub/blob/de1e56014cb0caf7e56de2320681781cae6a7e41/lib/data/lessons/lesson_tracing.dart#L1108>; ਘ: GNPS, Gurmukhi Sikho (GNPS Learning Hub), Alphabet Tracing lesson, ਘ (ghaggaa) checkpoints, strokes 1–2 (lib/data/lessons/lesson_tracing.dart line 276, commit de1e560; Apache-2.0) <https://github.com/codemanxdev/gnps_learning_hub/blob/de1e56014cb0caf7e56de2320681781cae6a7e41/lib/data/lessons/lesson_tracing.dart#L276>; ਦ: GNPS, Gurmukhi Sikho (GNPS Learning Hub), Alphabet Tracing lesson, ਦ (daddaa) checkpoints, strokes 1–2 (lib/data/lessons/lesson_tracing.dart line 730, commit de1e560; Apache-2.0) <https://github.com/codemanxdev/gnps_learning_hub/blob/de1e56014cb0caf7e56de2320681781cae6a7e41/lib/data/lessons/lesson_tracing.dart#L730>. Source notes on variation: ੜ: GNPS's children's Punjabi app (Apache-2.0; developer CodeManX) has a tracing lesson whose checkpoints the developer entered over the Noto Sans Gurmukhi letter, one list per pen-down stroke, and whose trace widget makes the child reach them in order. It writes ੜ in three pen-down strokes: the headline from left to right; then from the top right down to the left, clockwise round the knob and the right side, and left along the base to the bottom left; then the short right leg, down to the right. The headline first is the source's teaching order. Fluent writers are often described as adding the headline last (Alfaazo's general guidance on Gurmukhi; native Devanagari writers do so in HP Labs India's pen data), so the path shows how this lesson teaches the letter, not how every fluent hand writes it. The outline prints the knob as a solid teardrop, so the path loops clockwise inside it. Omniglot (Lake, Salakhutdinov & Tenenbaum, Science 350:1332, 2015; https://github.com/brendenlake/omniglot, MIT licence) holds 20 drawings of ੜ, each by a different non-native copyist; only counts and shares are cited. 65% (13 of 20) draw it in three strokes, the source's count and their most common one. For the first stroke of the body, 70% (14 of 20) start in the same part of the letter as the source and 85% (17 of 20) set off in the same direction, within 45 degrees. Only the order, the start, the direction and the lifts are taken from the source; no checkpoint coordinate is copied, and the path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Gurmukhi outline. Handwriting varies by writer. ਘ: GNPS's children's Punjabi app (Apache-2.0; developer CodeManX) has a tracing lesson whose checkpoints the developer entered over the Noto Sans Gurmukhi letter, one list per pen-down stroke, and whose trace widget makes the child reach them in order. It writes ਘ in two pen-down strokes: from the top left along the bar's left part, down and counterclockwise through the left bowl, the middle upright and the right bowl, ending on the right where the body meets the stem; then from the top right, left along the bar's right part and down the stem. In the bundled Noto Sans Gurmukhi outline this letter's top bar is split, with a gap above the body, and the source draws no separate headline: the first stroke opens along the bar's left part and the last stroke opens by running right to left along its right part before turning down the stem. The outline and the source agree, so there is no headline stroke to place first or last. The outline prints the middle upright as one solid shape, so the path loops up inside it counterclockwise and comes back down. Omniglot (Lake, Salakhutdinov & Tenenbaum, Science 350:1332, 2015; https://github.com/brendenlake/omniglot, MIT licence) holds 20 drawings of ਘ, each by a different non-native copyist; only counts and shares are cited. 50% (10 of 20) draw it in two strokes, the source's count and their most common one. For the first stroke of the body, 90% (18 of 20) start in the same part of the letter as the source and 50% (10 of 20) set off in the same direction, within 45 degrees. Only the order, the start, the direction and the lifts are taken from the source; no checkpoint coordinate is copied, and the path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Gurmukhi outline. Handwriting varies by writer. ਦ: GNPS's children's Punjabi app (Apache-2.0; developer CodeManX) has a tracing lesson whose checkpoints the developer entered over the Noto Sans Gurmukhi letter, one list per pen-down stroke, and whose trace widget makes the child reach them in order. It writes ਦ in two pen-down strokes: the headline from left to right; then from the top right down the stem, left along the bar, clockwise round the knob, and down and round to the bottom right. The headline first is the source's teaching order. Fluent writers are often described as adding the headline last (Alfaazo's general guidance on Gurmukhi; native Devanagari writers do so in HP Labs India's pen data), so the path shows how this lesson teaches the letter, not how every fluent hand writes it. The outline prints the knob as a solid teardrop, so the path loops clockwise inside it. Omniglot (Lake, Salakhutdinov & Tenenbaum, Science 350:1332, 2015; https://github.com/brendenlake/omniglot, MIT licence) holds 20 drawings of ਦ, each by a different non-native copyist; only counts and shares are cited. 65% (13 of 20) draw it in two strokes, the source's count and their most common one. For the first stroke of the body, 70% (14 of 20) start in the same part of the letter as the source and 90% (18 of 20) set off in the same direction, within 45 degrees. Only the order, the start, the direction and the lifts are taken from the source; no checkpoint coordinate is copied, and the path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Gurmukhi outline. Handwriting varies by writer.
svg.text: How it is written — 3 letters, one after another
Letter 1 of 3 — 3 strokes · 2 pen lifts · 7 movements
Letter 2 of 3 — 2 strokes · 1 pen lift · 6 movements
Letter 3 of 3 — 2 strokes · 1 pen lift · 5 movements
Letter 1: stroke order after GNPS, Gurmukhi Sikho (GNPS Learning Hub), Alphabet Tracing lesson, ੜ (rhaarhaa) checkpoints, strokes 1–3 (lib/data/lessons/lesson_tracing.dart line 1108,
Letter 2: stroke order after GNPS, Gurmukhi Sikho (GNPS Learning Hub), Alphabet Tracing lesson, ਘ (ghaggaa) checkpoints, strokes 1–2 (lib/data/lessons/lesson_tracing.dart line 276,
Letter 3: stroke order after GNPS, Gurmukhi Sikho (GNPS Learning Hub), Alphabet Tracing lesson, ਦ (daddaa) checkpoints, strokes 1–2 (lib/data/lessons/lesson_tracing.dart line 730,
This order is attested, not standardised; the source records where it varies.
